headline_summary: Nebius Group is the Netherlands-domiciled successor to Yandex N.V., reborn through a 2024 corporate restructuring that separated the Russian operating business and refocused the surviving NASDAQ-listed parent on AI infrastructure. Founder Arkady Volozh returned as CEO in 2024. FY2025 produced Q4 revenue $227.7M (+547% YoY), core AI cloud +802%, ARR $1.25B exit-2025, cash $3.7B, capex ~$2B Q4 alone, 170MW power active vs 2GW+ contracted. FY2026 guidance is the most aggressive in the peer set: revenue $3-3.4B, capex $16-20B, ARR $7-9B with >50% contracted, connected power 800MW-1GW.
headquarters: Amsterdam, Netherlands (corporate domicile); European data center footprint with US expansion underway
founded_as_yandex: 2000 (CompTek incubator 1990); Yandex NV IPO 2011; restructured to Nebius Group N.V. 2024
chairman: John Boynton (Independent Non-Executive Chairman; on board since 2000, chairman since 2016)
strategic_financing_2025: $700M oversubscribed equity placement from Accel + Nvidia + Orbis (August 2025); Matt Weigand joined board
structural_thesis_in_one_paragraph: Nebius compresses three distinct equity stories into one ticker: a corporate-restructuring outcome (Netherlands holdco that retains international assets after the Russian operating business sale), a balance-sheet rebuild (from post-restructuring uncertainty to $3.7B cash + $834M Q4 operating cash flow), and an AI-infrastructure capacity ramp targeting the most aggressive FY2026 guidance any AI-cloud company has publicly committed to. The investment question is whether Volozh's team can convert >50%-contracted FY26 ARR into deployed capacity inside the guidance window, against competition from CoreWeave / Lambda / Crusoe / hyperscaler-internal AI cloud capacity, while maintaining the Nvidia strategic-supplier-and-investor alignment that the $700M placement formalised.
